name: TMAG5273A1QDBVR
title: Low-power linear 3D Hall-effect sensor with I2C
summary: The TMAG5273 measures the magnetic field along X, Y and Z with three Hall elements and its own temperature, converts them with a 12-bit ADC and reports them over I2C at up to 1 MHz with optional CRC. An on-chip CORDIC turns any two axes into a 0 to 360° angle with gain and offset correction. Power modes run from 2.3 mA active down to 5 nA sleep, with a timed wake-up and sleep mode that interrupts the host on a field or temperature threshold. Eight versions combine two field ranges with four factory I2C addresses.
key_figures: 1 MHz max (VCC 2.3 V to 3.6 V), 400 kHz (1.7 V to 3.6 V)

circuits.title: Typical application
circuits.description: The sensor runs from a 1.7 V to 3.6 V rail with one capacitor from VCC to ground; TEST is grounded. SDA, SCL and INT each have a pull-up to the microcontroller's own 1.2 V to 5.5 V rail and run straight to the microcontroller. The angle-measurement application uses the same circuit with a TMAG5273A1 at 3.3 V.
notes: The decoupling capacitor is ceramic, at least 0.01 µF, close to VCC.

circuits.title: Magnetic tamper detection with battery back-up
circuits.description: An AC-DC converter and a back-up battery feed a power multiplexer whose output is the one 3.3 V rail for both the TMAG5273A2 and the microcontroller; the multiplexer also reports to the microcontroller whether mains power is present. The sensor has its decoupling capacitor and grounded TEST pin, SDA, SCL and INT are pulled up to the same rail, and the microcontroller has its own supply capacitor. On mains the sensor measures continuously; on battery it is put in wake-up and sleep mode and wakes the microcontroller through INT when a field crosses a threshold.
notes: Register settings on mains: DEVICE_CONFIG_1 = 1h, SENSOR_CONFIG_1 = 79h, T_CONFIG = 1h, INT_CONFIG_1 = A4h, DEVICE_CONFIG_2 = 22h; each INT low is followed by one 16-bit T, X, Y, Z read.
On loss of mains only two writes change: INT_CONFIG_1 = 64h, DEVICE_CONFIG_2 = 23h.

circuits.title: Four sensors on one I2C bus
circuits.description: Four TMAG5273A1 sensors share SDA, SCL and INT, each line with one pull-up to the 3.3 V rail. Each sensor is powered from its own microcontroller GPIO (5 mA per sensor) and has its own decoupling capacitor and grounded TEST pin. The GPIOs are turned on one at a time; after tstart_power_up the newly powered sensor is reached at the shared factory address and given a new one through I2C_ADDRESS before the next GPIO is turned on.
notes: With a shared INT line the microcontroller reads every sensor to find which one interrupted.
The address sequence is repeated after a power outage or a power-on reset.

operation.text: Three Hall elements (X, Y, Z) and a temperature sensor are multiplexed through one gain and filter stage into a single 12-bit ADC. A power block holds a low-power oscillator, a fast oscillator, biasing and undervoltage detection. The digital core holds configuration and result registers, the angle engine and the I2C interface with optional CRC.
A north pole brought near the part along an axis gives positive codes on that axis; a south pole from the same side gives negative codes.
The X, Y and Z elements sit together, 1.85 mm from the pin-1 end of the body along its length, 0.68 mm in from the side carrying pins 1 to 3, and 0.73 mm below the top of the package.

A conversion result or a threshold crossing can raise an interrupt, on INT or on SCL. On INT it is either a 10 µs pulse (INT_STATE = 1b) or a level held until the host addresses the part (INT_STATE = 0b). An SCL interrupt is a fixed 10 µs pulse driven on the clock line. After raising a threshold interrupt from wake-up and sleep mode the part returns to standby.

Each part answers at its factory address after power-up (A 35h, B 22h, C 78h, D 44h). The host can then write a new 7-bit address to I2C_ADDRESS with I2C_ADDRESS_UPDATE_EN set, giving up to 128 addresses; the new address does not survive a power cycle.

The part enters standby the first time it powers up, 270 µs after VCC passes its minimum. Oscillators and logic run and it waits for commands; a conversion is started by the trigger bit of an I2C command or by INT. The last results stay in the registers.

Sleep draws 5 nA typical and keeps the key configuration but not the results. I2C traffic or INT wakes it; standby is reached 50 µs later. Waking it through I2C pulses INT briefly; INT recovers once standby is reached, with RESULT_STATUS reading 0h. The part goes to sleep 20 µs after SCL goes high.

The part sleeps for the SLEEPTIME interval (1 ms to 20 s), wakes, measures and sleeps again. When a conversion meets the interrupt condition set in INT_CONFIG_1 it stores the data, leaves the cycle for standby and signals the host; otherwise the cycle repeats. The host can wake it at any time over I2C or INT. The conversion-complete interrupt does not work in this mode.

With OPERATING_MODE = 10b the part converts without pause using the SENSOR_CONFIG and DEVICE_CONFIG settings, and results can be read over I2C at any time. Hall spinning and integration of the next sample overlap the ADC conversion of the last. A temperature sample opens each conversion set and is used for magnet temperature compensation. Entering it from standby takes 70 µs.
With OPERATING_MODE = 00b one conversion set runs per trigger, given by I2C or by INT. A trigger arriving during a conversion waits for it to end; repeated triggers are ignored.

The XYX, YXY, YZY and XZX channel orders sample one axis on both sides of another, so the average of the outer pair lines up in time with the middle sample, which removes the timing error of a sequential angle measurement. The X and Y elements are vertical Hall elements and are noisier than the horizontal Z element, so taking two X or Y samples against one Z sample (XZX, YZY) evens out the noise.

Thresholds can be checked on one or several axes at once: above or below a level (MAG_THR_DIR with THR_HYST = 000b), or leaving or entering a band between equal positive and negative levels (THR_HYST = 001b). While the field stays in the flagged region, each new conversion raises another interrupt. THRX_COUNT can require four crossings before the interrupt.

A write is the address byte with R/W = 0, then a byte whose MSB is the conversion trigger and whose 7 LSBs are the start register, then data for consecutive registers. The general-call write uses address 00h to configure every device on the bus at once. The standard read writes the start register the same way, repeats the start with R/W = 1 and reads consecutive registers. The 1-byte read commands (I2C_RD = 01b or 10b) send only the address with R/W = 1 and return every enabled channel in the order T, X, Y, Z, 16 or 8 bits each, then CONV_STATUS.

With CRC_EN set a CRC byte follows the data of each read: after four register bytes in the standard read, and over the command byte and the data in the 1-byte reads. It uses x^8 + x^2 + x + 1 starting from FFh. On a bus with several devices the first CRC after switching to another device can be wrong.

Each axis and the temperature are 16-bit 2's complement values split over an MSB and an LSB register; reading only the MSB gives an 8-bit result. The angle is 13 bits: 9 integer bits (0 to 360) and 4 fraction bits, with the top three bits always zero.

For the pair of axes chosen by ANGLE_EN, MAG_OFFSET_CONFIG_1 and _2 subtract an offset from the first and second axis, both zero by default, and MAG_GAIN_CONFIG scales one axis by a fraction so both swing equally. For the on-axis case the magnitude stays constant over a full turn.

Use the most sensitive version and range that still covers the largest field the sensor will see, so the ADC span is used fully. Field strength rises steeply as a magnet comes closer, so a larger magnet further away can position more accurately than a small one close by.
MAG_TEMPCO corrects for a magnet whose remanence falls with temperature: about 0.12 %/°C for NdFeB and 0.20 %/°C for ferrite. Leave it at 00b when no compensation is wanted.

For a linear measurement the sensitivity error, offset and noise add as a root sum of squares. Cross-axis sensitivity and hysteresis are negligible for this sensor. A room-temperature calibration removes the 25 °C offset and sensitivity error, and up to 32x internal averaging, plus averaging in the host, reduces noise. Angle error also depends on axis mismatch, nonlinearity and drift over temperature and lifetime.

Any two axes chosen in ANGLE_EN feed the angle engine, which gives a full 360° result. On-axis mounting, directly under the magnet's axis, makes best use of the field and the ranges and is preferred where possible; off-axis mounting beside the magnet gives unequal axis amplitudes that the gain correction evens out. Gain correction also absorbs mechanical misalignment.
Result registers change at the end of each conversion, so reads must be timed to avoid one being overwritten mid-read; where timing is tight, use the conversion-complete interrupt on INT.
Place a ceramic decoupling capacitor of at least 0.01 µF close to VCC, and tie TEST to ground.
Fields pass with no significant change through plastic, aluminium and most circuit boards, so the magnet can sit outside an enclosure or on the far side of the board.

CONV_STATUS flags a power-on reset and any failed internal diagnostic (VCC undervoltage, memory CRC, INT pin, clock); DEVICE_STATUS names which one, each flag being cleared by writing 1, and reads back the INT pin level.
